question: Compare what the Matrice 30T and Matrice 4T manuals say happens if the pilot cancels low battery RTH.
stop_reason: claims still failing after the revision limit

intake.reason: Question asks for guidance from manuals on what happens when the pilot cancels a low-battery Return-to-Home (RTH) for the Matrice 30T and 4T; comparing documented behavior in manuals.

brief.short_answer: FAA guidance states that if a hazard arises from loss of control link, attempt to reestablish the control link. If the control link cannot be reestablished, start emergency or contingency procedures for loss of control link, and the remote PIC may need to land immediately, hover, or execute a return-to-home sequence. Manuals: there is no usable evidence for DJI Matrice 30T manual. Incident reports: there is no usable evidence for DJI Matrice 30T or 4T incident reports. Gap/conflict: there is no verified evidence in the Matrice 30T and 4T manuals about canceling low-battery RTH; FAA guidance discusses link recovery and contingency procedures.

decisions.new_text: Two or more certificated remote pilots transferring operational control (i.e., the remote PIC designation) to each other may do so only if they are both capable of maintaining Visual Line of Sight without loss of control (LOC).

AC 107-2A states that two or more certificated remote pilots transferring operational control to each other may do so only if they are both capable of maintaining Visual Line of Sight without loss of control.

C003.rationale: The cited passage explicitly states the preflight briefing must include control link loss procedures.
